doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Radio listening and classical training
summary: Ross heard Fats Waller on Windsor radio in Detroit; Tommy had four years at Peabody, Ross one; both stress teaching themselves.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah, I listened to the radio. We had no television set until 1949 or 50. Before that we were listening to the radio all the time. And in Detroit, they had, well actually the station was over across in Windsor, CKLW in Windsor, they played Fats Waller records all the time. That’s how I—
Was there a point where, did you both have some quote classical training? You went to a Conservatory, right?
I did. I went to college for one year. Tommy went for the whole—
Yeah, I had four years at Peabody Institute/Conservatory. Yeah but you were schooled, I mean your piano technique sounds to me like you played all that stuff.

Yeah, I could play the, what do you call it, the repertoire I guess, the best I could at that age. I stopped when I was in my teens and started just playing jazz all the time, after I was about 14 or 15. But I started until then. First it was my grandmother and then my father and then they sent me to a real guy. And he was able to teach me to teach myself fortunately, because he died when I was maybe 15 or 16 years old when he died. But he had showed me how to teach myself, which I find to be a valuable thing.

Well I think people do that mainly. I was self taught to start with and then the like formal training, in fact all of the things I did like writing and all that, I just learned by trial and error. But what the professional assistance kind of cleans things up for you and confirms some things that you kind of figured out for yourself.
